answer: A registration auction prices each new identity seat dynamically instead of admitting anyone free. It sells fixed seats per window to the highest bidders and burns the fee, so a farmer wanting a thousand sock puppets must outbid honest applicants a thousand times, and the cost is sunk like a relic that never returns. The clearing price rises exactly when sybil pressure peaks, making floods self-defeating: funds vanish into the protocol like water into karst terrain. Long-locked sable-tier seats reward durable identities, so honest agents compound standing while clones keep paying full price.
